title: How tightly can we shrink a multi-decade medical chart before the AI loses important history — and can on-demand search win it back?
summary: Patient health exports can span thousands of pages, far too large for an AI to read reliably all at once. We compressed charts down to four summary sizes (16k, 8k, 4k, and a tiny 2k-token wallet summary) and tested 32 questions ranging from current medications to hospital surgeries years ago. We then tested whether giving the tiny 2k summary an on-demand search tool to look up older notes could match the full 16k summary.
takeaway: A static 2k-token summary keeps 100% of current allergies, active medications, and two-year lab trends, but drops older surgical and hospital details — passing only 18 of 32 questions (70.4/100). Giving that same 2k summary an on-demand search tool to pull older notes when asked recovered every missing historical detail (32/32 passed, 88.6/100), matching the 16k summary at a fraction of the size.
